# WP2.5 - WP2 fixes and the layer framework (guide for the WP3 builders, notes for the Director)

Scope: `apps/desktop/client/src/**` only. No Rust, `bindings/`, `crates/`, `src-tauri/`, authority,
capability or mock change: `git diff --stat c4bbe5b -- crates bindings apps/desktop/src-tauri` is
empty. No dependency added.

## 1. What changed

### WP2 defects (Director review)
| # | Fix |
|---|---|
| A1 | The decision fills its column: `.cs-decision` is three groups spaced over the column (head; silence line + action; facts strip on the bottom edge). Display type steps through new tokens `--fs-hero` 34px / `--fs-hero-l` 44px / `--fs-hero-xl` 54px (`design/tokens.css`, never body text). The stack row gets a second row of cards on a tall, wide window (`stackRows(w, h)`, >= 1500 x 1000), so more of the queue is in view. Measured gaps between the groups: 1280x800 small 99 px / large 97 px; 1920x1080 small 89 px / large 81 px (was ~190 px band). |
| A2 | The countdown is its own non-wrapping chip after the "If you do nothing" sentence (`.cs-sil-cd`, tabular figures). |
| A3 | Charter fills the sheet: both columns run full height, the five lines share the right column, the current line's explanation sits beside its one action on wide windows, a "When you sign it, line I reads" preview (or "Signed: line II reads"), the note on the bottom edge, and the wallet's seal beside the current line (`Charter seal` prop; the setup layer sets `ownSeal` so the sheet's corner seal is not drawn twice). Left-column gaps: 1280 103 px, 1920 109 px (was ~220 px above and below). |
| A4 | `BeadStrip`: every bead is a `<button>` with a 24 px target around the small visual bead, named by the deal's plain title (state in its tooltip), one tab stop (roving tabindex), Arrow keys / Home / End move along it (handled there, so the centre's own Left/Right do not also run), Enter or click opens the deal. `DialStrip` (shared/brand) stays presentational by its WP1a contract and is unused by the app. |
| A5 | `ChromeBackContext` (shared/ui `DetailPage.tsx`): inside a console layer a `DetailPage` draws no Back of its own; the top bar's Back / Esc / crumbs are the only Back. The old module detail pages lose their second Back today. |

### Owner feedback applied
Rules, Connections, Settings, the pairing desk and the safety record are layers of the one main
window (same Calibre theme). `windows/main/Sheet.tsx` and `sheet.css` are deleted; the old
`SafetySheet` wrapper is gone (the `SafetyView` stays, tested). The Quit confirm and the keyboard
shortcuts help stay sheets (they are a confirm and a help overlay, not layers). The approval
window stays the only separate window. Hold stays Space-only (no change here).

Old links, still parsed (tested in `logic.test.ts`, `console/route.test.ts`): `#s=settings`,
`#s=pairing`, `#s=mandates` (the old sheet, over any route) open settings / pairing / rules;
`#<route>&p=safety` opens the safety record, from the module when the route was a module
(`#m=book&p=safety` -> `#p=safety&m=book`, the Director's beat). The first history entry is
rewritten to the canonical form. A place opened from inside a layer (`nav.place`) remembers where
it came from (a module page, or Settings); the top bar's Rules / Connections / Settings always open
one layer above the centre. Esc, Back, crumbs, browser Back/forward and focus/scroll restore are
WP2's, unchanged, and work for every place (tested: Rules -> Wallet limits -> Esc -> Esc, focus back
on the link and then the top-bar button).

## 3. The layer registry (how a WP3 area plugs in)

- `console/layers.tsx`: the types and the host. `LayerId`, `LayerDef { id, component, title(route),
  Crumb?, tone?, fit?, ownSeal? }`, `defineLayer`, `layerIdOf(route)`, `LayerNav`, `LayerState`,
  `useLayerNav()`, `useLayerState()`, `LayerHost` (per-layer `ErrorBoundary` + `Suspense` with the calm
  `LayerSkeleton`, which appears only after `--dur-slow`, so a fast chunk never flashes; provides
  `ModuleRouteContext` for module routes and `ChromeBackContext`).
- `console/layers.registry.ts`: one import line per area file; `layerOf(route)`, `LAYER_PARTS`
  (idle preload). `framework.test.tsx` checks every LayerId is registered exactly once.
- `console/layers/<area>.ts`: one file per WP3 area, already created and already registered:
  `tables spend counter book shield rescue deal rewind setup rules (rules + limits) connections
  (connections + pairing) settings safety`. Each currently points its `component` at an interim
  body in `console/legacy.tsx` (the old page inside the new chrome). **Your whole change to plug in
  is the `import(...)` target of your area file.** `layers/core.tsx` (centre, waiting) is the
  console's own, not a WP3 area.
- Parent and depth are not per-layer settings: they are derived from the route in one pure,
  tested place (`logic.ts stepBack`, `console/route.ts chainOf/depthOf`). That is deliberate
  (counter-proposal to "parent(route), depth(route) per entry"): parallel builders cannot make the
  chain disagree with Escape, crumbs or focus restore. A new nested level is a route change there.

Area file, after WP3 (example):
```ts
// console/layers/spend.ts
import { lazyPart } from '../../../../lib/lazy';
import { MODULE } from '../../../../shared/modules';
import { ModuleCrumb } from '../crumbs';
import { defineLayer, type LayerProps } from '../layers';
import { defineModuleViews } from '../ModuleSummary';
import '../areas/spend.css';

export const SPEND_VIEWS = defineModuleViews('spend', { recent: 'Recent purchases', limits: 'Limits' });
export const layers = [
  defineLayer({ id: 'spend', title: () => MODULE.spend.name, Crumb: ModuleCrumb,
    component: lazyPart<LayerProps>(() => import('../areas/spend/SpendLayer').then((m) => m.SpendLayer)) }),
];
```

`LayerNav` (the only moves a layer has): `go(route, {replace?, focus?})`, `back()`, `home()`,
`module(m)`, `deal(id)` (one layer below where it is opened), `need(dealId)` (the centre at that
decision), `place(p, {pair?})`, `rewind(at?)`, `setup(step?)`, `quit()`. None touches money.
`LayerState` (read-only): `rewindAt`, `pairMode`, `firstRun`, `presence` (the seal's state).

## 4. Building blocks

### ModuleLayer (`console/ModuleLayer.tsx`) + ModuleSummary (`console/ModuleSummary.tsx`)
```tsx
<ModuleLayer module="spend"
  answer={SPEND_ANSWER(n)}                 // the ONE answer line = the layer's h1 (focused going in)
  kicker={...}                             // default MODULE.spend.long
  yourCall={undefined}                     // default: this module's open decisions from the World
                                           // (count + the first one's "If you do nothing"); null hides
  action={<Btn kind="gold" ...>}           // at most one gold action; gold only for an approval_open hand-off
  cards={[{ id: 'recent', view: 'recent', label, value, note?, chip?, ifNothing? }]}   // 3-4; ifNothing on a needs-you card
  explain={{ summary: SPEND_WHY, body: <p>...</p> }}
  empty={SPEND_EMPTY}                      // one calm line when there are no cards and no children
  views={{ recent: { title: SPEND_VIEWS.recent, sub?, actions?, render: () => <ListEngine .../> } }}>
  {children /* the summary's list */}
</ModuleLayer>
```
A card opens its view through `useModuleRoute().open(view, cardId)`; coming back puts focus on the
card. Register view labels with `defineModuleViews` in the area file (so crumbs and Escape know
them before your chunk loads). A view is hosted under its own h1; never draw a Back.

### ListEngine (`console/ListEngine.tsx`)
```tsx
<ListEngine<Deal> label={...} rows={deals} getKey={(d) => d.id}
  searchText={(d) => `${title} ${counterparty}`}   // built once per rows change, lowercased; must depend on the row only
  filters={FILTERS} sorts={SORTS}                  // keep both arrays stable (module constants)
  estimateSize={48} /* or (row) => px, with measure */ measure
  renderRow={(d, { focused, selected }) => <DealRow deal={d} need={...} who={...} />}
  rowLabel={(d) => title} onOpen={(d) => nav.deal(d.id)}
  detail={(d) => <Pane/>}                          // >= 1500 px: picked row beside the list instead of opening
  empty={AREA_EMPTY} noMatch={AREA_NO_MATCH} />
```
Search debounced 120 ms; filter counts in one pass per data change (`countFilters`, tested: 5,000
rows x 2 filters = 10,000 tests, none again on re-render); counts through `formatCount` (99+);
"Showing N of M" via `formatTally`; toolbar hidden at <= 8 rows; rows are buttons (one tab stop,
arrows / Page / Home / End, Enter opens); Escape clears the search or filter first, then goes on to
the console (one layer up). `groupBy` is a reserved slot (typed, not drawn yet). The list needs a
bounded height: put it in a flex column (`.ml-body` / `.ml-vbody` are), or mark the layer `fit`.

### Row parts (`console/rows.tsx`)
`Amount { money | minor+currency, tone? }` (lib/format; unknown = dash), `StateChip { deal | state }`
(stateWord; an unknown state = dashed "Not available yet", never the raw name), `Countdown
{ deadline, ticking? }` (non-wrapping chip; no deadline said so), `WhoChip { name }` (truncates, full
name in the title; null = "not named yet"), `DealRow { deal, need?, who?, extra? }` (content only,
for inside a ListEngine row). Crumbs: `ModuleCrumb`, `DealCrumb` (`console/crumbs.tsx`).

### Worked example
`console/examples/ModuleExample.tsx`: a whole module layer from the World (ModuleLayer, Your call,
four cards opening two views, explanation, a measured ListEngine of DealRows with filters, sort and
the wide-window pane). Browser preview only: add `?framework-example` to the preview URL (any
module tab), e.g. `index.html?framework-example&scale=large#m=tables&v=ex-all`. Never in the shell.

## 5. Conventions for parallel builders
- **Your files**: `console/layers/<area>.ts`, `console/areas/<area>.css` (imported only by your area
  file; scope rules under your own root class, tokens only, motion only via `--dur-*`/`--ease-*`),
  `lib/words/<area>.ts` (re-exported from `lib/words.ts` by one `export *` line already; prefix your
  exports with the area, a duplicate name across areas is a type error), and anything new under
  `console/areas/<area>/`. Do not edit `legacy.tsx`, `layers.tsx`, `layers.registry.ts`,
  `framework.css`, `Console.tsx`, `lib/words.ts` or another area's files; ask the Director.
- No `useWorld()` in new code (narrow selectors: `useNeeds`, `useDeals`, `useDisplayOf`, ...).
- Money: only `approval_open` leads to approval (the guard test reads every file under
  windows/main); amounts only through `Amount`/lib/format; never parse rendered text.
- No innerHTML, no `window.*` globals, no magic delays (motion tokens), no optimistic outcomes.
- Every needs-you view says "If you do nothing"; unknown values are dashed, never 0 or green;
  never show internals (commands, ids, clause numbers, raw states).
- One gold action per view; light theme at 1280x800 must work.

## 6. Tests and the scale smoke harness
- `console/testing/scaleSmoke.tsx`: `renderLayerAtScale(route | hash | (world) => Promise<Route>,
  'small' | 'large')` renders the whole window on the mock world and returns `{ layer, errors,
  calls, texts(), rows(), ms, budget }`; `expectLayerHealthy(run, { maxRows?, maxDisplays?, maxMs? })`
  checks no console error, no raw enum/id text (`RAW_TEXT`), list rows in the DOM <= 250, world
  reads once, displays <= 500, <= 16 reads in flight, only reads and `approval_open` sent. In your
  test file: `vi.mock('<path>/lib/runtime', async () => (await import('<path>/console/testing/runtime')).runtimeMock);`
- `console/scaleSmoke.test.tsx` runs it for all 16 registered layers at large, a deal, and the small centre.
- New: `console/framework.test.tsx` (registry, host owns Back, boundary fallback, ModuleLayer,
  row parts), `console/ListEngine.test.tsx` (5,000 rows), console.test.tsx "the owner places are
  layers" (3 tests), route/logic tests extended, `stackRows`.
